keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Area check: neither page gives an area. The page describes only a state 'centered around the city of Mantua in Lombardy'; Gianfrancesco added 'border lands of today's Upper Mantua area, taken from the Brescians' and 'the territories of Ostiano and Isola Dovarese, wrested from the Cremonese' (undated), which lie partly outside the modern province. Mantua province (about 2,340 km2) is a reading for the whole life; Montferrat is a vassal from 1536 (see the ledger).

region.text: Mantua province, the state 'centered around the city of Mantua in Lombardy'

ledger.note: 16 August 1328: the Gonzaga seize Mantua. 'On 16 August 1328, the last Bonacolsi, Rinaldo, was overthrown in a revolt backed by the House of Gonzaga'; Ludovico 'was elected capitano del popolo'. The land is my reading (the city and its province).
22 September 1433: Mantua becomes a marquisate. Infobox: 'Imperial diploma of Sigismund of Bohemia: 22 September 1433'; Gianfrancesco 'in 1433 was appointed first marquis by the Emperor Sigismund'.
8 April 1530: Charles V raises Mantua to a duchy. Infobox: 'Margravate of Mantua is raised to Duchy: 8 April 1530' (the Marquisate page's text has 25 March 1530).

union.text: the provinces of Alessandria and Asti, 'roughly' Montferrat

ledger.note: 1536: Montferrat passes to Duke Federico II of Mantua. Charles V 'restored it to Federico II, Duke of Mantua from the House of Gonzaga in 1536'; the Duchy of Mantua page has 'In 1531, the duchy also acquired the March of Montferrat, thanks to the marriage between Gonzaga and Margaret Paleologa'. Modelled as a personal union, drawn as the lighter vassal tint.

region.text: Mantua, taken by the Imperial army

ledger.note: 18 July 1630: Imperial troops take and sack Mantua. 'it surrendered to Gallas and Aldringen on 18 July'; 'an Imperial army of 36,000 Landsknecht mercenaries besieged Mantua, bringing the plague with them'. [Reviewer eu-13-x, 2026-10-31: counterpart was holy-roman-empire, whose dossier ends in 1259; the Empire after 1260 is holy-roman-empire-minor-states.]

wars.name: War of the Mantuan Succession
wars.outcome: After the Gonzaga line ended in December 1627 Charles of Nevers claimed Mantua and Montferrat against Spain, Savoy and the Emperor; Imperial troops took Mantua on 18 July 1630 and the Treaty of Cherasco (19 June 1631) confirmed Nevers. [Reviewer eu-13-x, 2026-10-31: from 1627 to 1628 (page infobox and lead: 1628-1631); the Empire after 1259 is holy-roman-empire-minor-states.]
wars.note: The infobox gives 1628-1631; Vincenzo II died in December 1627. Ledger events for Montferrat's sieges are in marquisate-of-montferrat.

notes: Written from five pages (two shared with the Montferrat dossier). Mantua is the Gonzaga state from the 1328 revolt, so the marquisate (1433) and duchy (1530) are rename events, not separate dossiers; the Duchy page's 'disestablished 1797' covers the Austrian period after 1708, which is the Habsburg dossier's (eu-09). Montferrat is a separate dossier (marquisate-of-montferrat) drawn here as a vassal from 1536 to 1708 (a modelling choice for the personal union). Unsettled: the Mantuan extent (no area on either page; the border lands taken from Brescia and Cremona under Gianfrancesco are undated), the Gonzaga of Guastalla and Sabbioneta (separate branches, not on the pages opened), the 1707-1708 Imperial occupation in the Spanish Succession war (the page says only that Ferdinando Carlo allied with France), the 1531 against 1536 date for Montferrat. Page budget: the Treaty of Cherasco has no page of its own here.
